;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**The [[Syrian Army]] and allied militia groups secure the entire length of the strategic [[Transport_in_Syria#Motorways|M5 Motorway]], connecting [[Damascus]] and [[Aleppo]], for the first time since 2012. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-syria-security-turkey/syrian-govt-seizes-idlib-highway-as-turkey-russia-talks-end-idUKKBN2050QN?il=0 (Reuters)]
**A [[Syrian Air Force]] [[Mil Mi-17|Mi-17]] helicopter is shot down by [[Turkey|Turkish]]-backed rebel forces near the village of [[Nayrab, Idlib|Nayrab]] in [[Idlib Governorate]], killing both pilots. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/syria/turkey-backed-rebels-down-syrian-army-helicopter-report-says-1.8523125 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[February 2020 Kabul bombing]]
**A [[suicide bombing]] in [[Afghanistan]]'s capital [[Kabul]] kills six people and injures twelve others. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/11/dead-suicide-attack-on-kabul-military-academy-afghanistan-taliban (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 Iranian attack on U.S. forces in Iraq]]
**[[The Pentagon]] confirms that the number of [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] who suffered [[traumatic brain injuries]] from the [[Iran]]ian attacks in January is higher than previously stated, now being at 109. [https://www.dw.com/en/109-us-service-members-were-injured-in-the-iran-missile-attack/a-52331039 (DW)]
*[[2019–20 Lebanese protests]]
**[[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] [[protester]]s attempt to block a [[Motion of no confidence|confidence vote]], and 400 people are injured.  The Lebanese Cabinet wins the vote. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/lebanon-protesters-try-to-block-confidence-vote/ar-BBZSsdX (MSN)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/lebanese-cabinet-wins-confidence-vote-despite-protesters-rioting-outside-parliament-n1135031 (NBC)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show]]
**Siba, a standard [[Poodle]], wins [[List of Best in Show winners of the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show|Best in Show Award]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/lifestyle/poodle-wins-best-in-show-at-westminster (Fox News)] [https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/28683375/siba-standard-poodle-wins-westminster-best-show (ESPN)] [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2020/feb/11/westminster-kennel-club-dog-show-2020-live (''The Guardian'')]

;Business and economy
*''[[New York v. Deutsche Telekom]]''
**[[Victor Marrero]], a [[United States district court|U.S. District Judge]] for the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York|Southern District of New York]], approves the $26 billion [[United States dollar|USD]] merger of [[T-Mobile US]] and [[Sprint Corporation]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/judge-approves-26-billion-merger-t-mobile-sprint-n1134631 (NBC)]
*[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] approves the [[High Speed 2]] railway project, after many delays and the project going billions of [[Pound sterling|pounds]] overbudget. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/feb/11/boris-johnson-bets-on-hs2-to-deliver-new-spine-of-uk-transport (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Softbank]], the Japanese [[venture capital]] giant, announced fourth quarter results. They were dismal, due especially to Softbank's losses on its [[Vision Fund]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-softbank-group-results/softbank-profit-wiped-out-by-vision-fund-losses-second-fund-scaled-back-idUSKBN2060JB (Reuters)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Storm Ciara]] kills six people in Europe. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/storm-ciara-kills-at-least-six-in-europe/ar-BBZSqdh (MSN)]
*A boat carrying [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] refugees capsizes in the [[Bay of Bengal]] while trying to reach [[Malaysia]]. Fifteen are confirmed dead and dozens are missing, a [[Bangladesh Coast Guard]] official says. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-rohingya-accident/dozens-of-rohingya-refugees-missing-15-confirmed-dead-after-boat-capsizes-idUSKBN2050G2 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****The death toll of the [[coronavirus]] outbreak in [[China]] surpasses 1,000. [[Hubei province]] reported 103 deaths in a single day, the highest single-day toll of the pandemic. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-death-toll-surpasses-1000/a-52331166 (DW)]
**The [[World Health Organization]] announces that the new coronavirus will be called [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/02/11/world-health-organization-names-the-new-coronavirus-covid-19.html (CNBC)]

;International relations
*[[Philippines–United States relations]]
**The [[President of the Philippines]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] terminates the [[Visiting Forces Agreement (Philippines – United States)|Visiting Forces Agreement]] with the [[United States]]. [[Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Philippines)|Foreign Secretary]] [[Teodoro Locsin Jr.]] confirms that the [[Embassy of the United States, Manila]], has been formally notified. The termination will take effect after 180 days. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippined-usa-defence/philippines-to-terminate-troop-agreement-with-u-s-idUSKBN2050E9 (Reuters)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/11/philippines-to-terminate-troop-agreement-with-us (''The Guardian'')]
*Aftermath of the [[Sudanese Revolution]]
**[[Sudan]]'s ruling military council agrees to hand over ousted dictator [[Omar al-Bashir]] to the [[International Criminal Court]] in [[The Hague]] to face charges of [[crimes against humanity]] in [[Darfur]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/11/sudan-says-it-will-send-former-dictator-omar-al-bashir-to-icc (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*''[[Love v Commonwealth]]''
**The [[High Court of Australia]] finds that [[Aboriginal Australians|Aboriginal Australian]] people are not "aliens" under the [[Constitution of Australia|Australian Constitution]], even if they were not born in Australia and do not have [[Australian citizenship]], and they cannot be [[deport]]ed. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-02-11/high-court-rules-aboriginal-people-cant-be-deported/11953012 (ABC News)] [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/high-court-rules-aboriginal-australians-cannot-be-aliens-under-the-constitution (SBS News)]
*[[Venezuela]] makes its [[National Bolivarian Militia of Venezuela|civilian militia]] a new branch of the [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|armed forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-military/venezuela-makes-civilian-militia-part-of-armed-forces-idUSKBN20526R?il=0 (Reuters)]

It comes after the [[2020 Iowa Democratic caucuses|controversial Iowa caucuses]] that occurred a week earlier.
